title: Skillet-Roasted Whole Fish with Burst Tomatoes, Olives & Garlic Crostini
dek: A whole Mediterranean-style fish roasts over blistered cherry tomatoes and olives, then comes to the table with lemon, fresh herbs and crisp garlic-rubbed bread.
image_alt: Whole roasted fish in a black skillet with blistered cherry tomatoes, black olives, lemon, basil, thyme and two garlic crostini
ingredients: 1 whole cleaned and scaled round fish, 2 to 2 1/2 lb (branzino, sea bream or red snapper), fins trimmed
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
6 fresh thyme sprigs, plus more for serving
1/2 cup pitted Kalamata or other black olives
1/4 cup dry white wine or low-sodium vegetable broth
4 slices baguette, each about 1/2 inch thick
1/3 cup loosely packed fresh basil leaves

instructions.name: Heat the oven and dry the fish
instructions.text: Set a rack in the middle of the oven and heat to 450°F. Confirm that the fish is gutted, scaled and has no sharp fins. Pat the cavity and skin very dry with paper towels; do not rinse raw fish. Cut three shallow diagonal slashes through the skin on each side without cutting to the bone.

instructions.name: Season the fish inside and out
instructions.text: Season the cavity and both sides with 1 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cut half the lemon into thin rounds and tuck them into the cavity with four thyme sprigs and one thinly sliced garlic clove. Rub the skin with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

instructions.name: Blister the tomatoes and olives
instructions.text: Heat a 12-inch ovenproof cast-iron or stainless-steel skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil, the tomatoes, olives, remaining two thyme sprigs, optional red pepper flakes, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and remaining 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan twice, until several tomatoes blister but most remain whole.

instructions.name: Roast to a safe center
instructions.text: Push the tomatoes and olives toward the skillet edges and lay the fish in the center. Pour the wine or broth around, not over, the fish. Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast for 18 to 25 minutes. Begin checking at 18 minutes: the thickest flesh just behind the head should reach 145°F without the thermometer touching bone, look opaque and lift cleanly from the backbone.

instructions.name: Make the garlic crostini
instructions.text: While the fish roasts, arrange the baguette slices on a small sheet pan. Brush both sides with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Bake on a lower rack for 5 to 7 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden at the edges. Halve one garlic clove and rub its cut side lightly over each hot toast.

instructions.name: Rest and finish
instructions.text: Remove the skillet carefully and rest the fish for 5 minutes; the handle will be extremely hot. Squeeze the unused lemon half over the tomatoes, then scatter the basil and extra thyme around the fish. Drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil.

instructions.name: Serve from the skillet
instructions.text: Set two crostini beside the fish in the skillet to match the photograph and serve the other two separately. Lift off the top fillet, remove the backbone in one piece, then portion the bottom fillet, checking each serving for small bones. Spoon the burst tomatoes, olives and pan juices over the fish.

why_it_works: Drying and lightly scoring the skin helps it tighten without tearing as the thick center cooks through.
Blistering the tomatoes before the fish enters the oven starts their sauce while preserving the whole red tomatoes visible around the finished fish.
A small amount of wine or broth creates savory pan juices without submerging the fish or softening all of its skin.
Measuring the flesh beside the head targets the slowest-cooking area; avoiding the bone prevents a falsely high thermometer reading.
Garlic-rubbed crostini provide a crisp tool for the tomato-olive juices and reproduce the two toasted bread slices visible in the photograph.
swaps: Use any cleaned round fish in the 2 to 2 1/2 pound range, such as branzino, sea bream or red snapper. A thicker fish may need several extra minutes; temperature and texture, not species, determine doneness.

For fillets, use four 5- to 6-ounce skin-on white-fish fillets. Blister the tomatoes first, nestle in the fillets and roast 8 to 12 minutes to 145°F; the presentation will differ from the whole-fish photograph.
Use low-sodium vegetable broth instead of wine. Add 1 teaspoon white-wine vinegar with the final lemon to replace some of the wine's acidity.
Castelvetrano olives can replace black olives for a milder flavor, though the garnish color will not match the photograph.
storage: Remove leftover flesh from the bones within 2 hours and refrigerate it with the tomato-olive mixture in a shallow airtight container for up to 2 days. Refrigerate crostini separately and re-crisp them at 350°F for 4 to 6 minutes. Reheat fish and vegetables covered at 300°F with 1 tablespoon broth until the center reaches 165°F. Freezing is not recommended because whole roasted fish becomes dry and the tomatoes turn watery.
notes: Ask the fish counter to gut, scale and trim the fins. A 2- to 2 1/2-pound fish fits a typical 12-inch skillet and yields four modest servings after bones and head are removed.
Fish thickness matters more than its total weight. Start checking early and insert the thermometer horizontally into the thickest flesh just behind the gill plate.
Keep a dry oven mitt over or beside the skillet handle after it leaves the oven so nobody mistakes the handle for a cool stovetop handle.
Calories and cost include one crostini per serving. Fish prices vary widely by species and region, so the cost estimate assumes a moderately priced whole farmed fish.

faqs.q: How do I know when a whole roasted fish is done?
faqs.a: Check the thickest flesh just behind the head. It should register 145°F without the probe touching bone, turn opaque and release from the backbone with gentle pressure. Clear eyes or browned skin alone are not reliable doneness tests.

faqs.q: Do I need to flip the fish while it roasts?
faqs.a: No. The hot skillet conducts heat into the underside while the 450°F oven cooks the top. Flipping a tender whole fish risks tearing its skin and breaking the fillets before serving.

faqs.q: Can I prepare this whole fish ahead?
faqs.a: You can clean, dry and season the fish up to 4 hours ahead and keep it uncovered on a tray in the refrigerator. Slice the garlic and prepare the tomatoes and olives separately. Cook only when ready to serve, because reheated whole fish loses moisture quickly.
